newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Volga-Dnepr air cargo sales, loads up.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Volga-Dnepr air cargo sales, loads up.

text.p: Sales of Russian cargo airline AO Volga-Dnepr over the first 11 months of the year rose to $95 million from $73 million over the same period in 1995, a company spokesman said on Monday.

Konstantin Rogov told Reuters by telephone from the central Russian city of Ulyanovsk that Volga-Dnepr carried 38,825 tonnes of cargo between January and November of 1996 against 34,943 in the first 11 months of 1995.

Operations with Antonov An-124-100 heavy cargo aircraft accounted for $86.9 million of the company's $95 million sales between January and November, up from 40 percent of sales over that period in 1995.
He said Volga-Dnepr held 60 per cent of global shipments in the super-heavyweight load sector, over 120 tonnes.
"But our Antonov-12 and An-32 fleet's sales volume fell 40 percent during eleven months of this year," Rogov said, referring to light cargo planes.

Ulyanovsk-based Volga-Dnepr, operates 12 cargo planes -- seven An-124s, three Il-76TDs, one An-12 and one An-32 freighter. It uses a Yakovlev-40 jet for regular passenger flights between Ulyanovsk and Moscow.
The company had sales of $87.2 million in 1995 compared with $87.8 million in 1994.
